name: Holographic
basis: iridescence faked as a hue from brightness, position and time (how)
note: Imitates a material (diffraction foil) but models no making process and no diffraction.

lumenary.blurb: Iridescent foil that shifts with a moving light band. Hover to steer it.

why: Holographic foil is covered in microscopic grooves that split light into colours, so the colour you see depends on the angle you look from. A screen has no angle, so this treatment makes up a stand-in coordinate from brightness, position and time and reads a rainbow from it. Because brightness is part of the coordinate, the rainbow follows the shapes in your picture.
how: Mix three things into one coordinate: the pixel’s brightness, its position across a tilted axis, and time.
Wrap the coordinate into the range 0 to 1 and use it as a hue, looked up in a table of 512 saturated colours.
Mix the foil colour with the base picture by the intensity slider, weighted by brightness so shadows stay dark.
Sweep a soft white band, shaped like a Gaussian bell, across the tilted axis. Hovering moves it to the cursor.
Every tenth of a second, set a tiny random share of the brighter pixels to white for sparkle.
history: Dennis Gabor invented holography in 1947 and won the Nobel Prize for it in 1971. Embossed holograms became familiar on credit cards in the 1980s as a hard-to-copy security feature. Iridescent foil later spread to packaging, trading cards and fashion, and had a strong revival in the 2010s.
uses: Trading card and sticker style art
Poster and cover art with a shimmer
terms: Colour that changes with the viewing angle.
A surface with fine grooves that splits light into its colours.
paragraphs: Real holographic foil changes colour with the viewing angle. Here the “angle” is replaced by a coordinate that mixes three things: the pixel’s own brightness, its position across a tilted axis, and time. That coordinate is wrapped into the range 0 to 1 and used as a hue, looked up in a precomputed table of 512 fully saturated colours. Because brightness is part of the coordinate, the rainbow follows the shapes in your picture rather than lying on top of it like a gradient.

The foil colour is mixed with the base picture (greyscale or original) in proportion to the intensity slider, and weighted by brightness so shadows stay dark. A soft white band, shaped like a Gaussian bell across the tilted axis, sweeps over the surface; hovering moves it to the cursor. Finally, sparkle sets a tiny random fraction of the brighter pixels to white every tenth of a second, using a coordinate hash so each frame’s glitter is different but cheap.

equations.note: Hue of the foil at a pixel: brightness L, spread σ, position along the tilted axis, drift τ.
Mix of base picture and foil; k is the intensity slider.
The moving light band: a Gaussian of width w centred at position p.

presets.text: Spread the colours wide for a full rainbow across the picture.
Keep the original colours under the foil for a subtler sheen.
Turn the sparkle up for glitter foil.
